il_f_shadow_of_a_man_area.blurb: A cluster of sandstone boulders in the Holy Boulders of southern Illinois, a short walk beyond the Mollusk boulder where the trail meets the cliffline and splits. The 22 problems cover nearly the whole difficulty range: a handful of easy slabs near the bottom, a solid middle of V2 to V5 lines, and a harder tier reaching V7. That mix makes it a good stop for a mixed group, with warm-ups and projects within a few steps of each other. Expect friction-dependent faces and aretes of modest height, so a couple of pads and a spotter are worthwhile. The big flagship boulder is hard to miss from the path, and nearby clusters are close enough to link into a longer session.

il_v_atlas_boulder_and_surrounding.blurb: A big sandstone boulder sitting almost on the main trail through the Holy Boulders, with a few smaller blocks around it. Its 20 problems run from easy warm-ups up to V6, though most of the weight is in the V0 to V4 range, so it suits climbers building up to harder boulders. The most sought-after lines are on the tall cliff-facing side of the main block; the rest are shorter faces, aretes and a chimney. Because it lies beside the path, it is a convenient first or last stop of the day. It is also the jumping-off point for the trail down toward Red Sea Boulder, a few minutes farther south.

il_c_red_sea_boulder.blurb: A large sandstone boulder beside the power line clearing at the Holy Boulders in southern Illinois. It is the hard-climber's stop in this part of the property: of its 20 problems, only a few are below V5, and the rest climb through V6 to V8 with several lines in the V9 to V12 range. That makes it a place for projecting rather than warming up, so bring your easier circuit from elsewhere. Reach it by following the main path south past the Shadow of a Man and Atlas boulders, then dropping down a worn trail behind Atlas; allow roughly five minutes from there.

il_j_tyler_durden_area.blurb: A small sandstone sector of the Holy Boulders in southern Illinois, centred on a sizable boulder at the edge of a clearing along the trail from the Mollusk boulder, about five minutes in. The 20 problems skew gentle: most fall between V0 and V2, which makes it one of the friendlier stops on the property for newer boulderers and for warming up. A few harder lines go up through V5, with one V7 and one V8 for those who want a project. It is not a huge concentration of problems, but the ones here are well regarded, and a shorter block farther along the path adds some easy climbs.

il_c_applejack_wall.blurb: A sandstone wall in the West Falls section of Jackson Falls canyon in southern Illinois, just beyond the Group Therapy wall near The Gallery. It holds 21 routes, nearly all of them bolted, plus a couple of trad lines including a crack. The grades lean hard: a single 5.8, two in the 5.10s, and the bulk between 5.11 and 5.13, so it is mostly a destination for strong sport climbers. Newer lines continue down toward the falls past the far end of the wall. The walk from the trail is a short dirt path directly to the base.
